name: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Budapest Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for CRPS (IASP 2012)

criteria.description: Continuing pain disproportionate to any inciting event
Sensory: reports of hyperesthesia and/or allodynia
Vasomotor: reports of temperature asymmetry and/or skin color changes
Sudomotor/edema: reports of edema and/or sweating changes
Motor/trophic: reports of decreased range of motion and/or motor dysfunction and/or trophic changes (hair, nail, skin)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Continuing pain disproportionate to event. Must report symptoms in at least 3 of 4 categories (sensory, vasomotor, sudomotor/edema, motor/trophic) AND display signs at time of evaluation in at least 2 of 4 categories. No other diagnosis better explains the findings.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Type I (no definable nerve injury, formerly RSD) vs Type II (with definable nerve injury, formerly causalgia). Budapest criteria have ~99% specificity.

laboratory: Routine labs normal; used to exclude inflammatory or infectious causes
imaging: Triple-phase bone scan: increased uptake in affected limb (sensitivity ~50%)
X-ray: patchy osteopenia/demineralization of affected limb (Sudeck atrophy)
MRI: bone marrow edema, soft tissue edema, skin thickening in affected region
genetic: HLA associations reported (HLA-DQ1, HLA-B62) but not diagnostic
other: Quantitative sensory testing (QST): demonstrates allodynia and hyperalgesia
Infrared thermography: temperature asymmetry > 1°C between limbs
Budapest clinical criteria are primary diagnostic tool (no single confirmatory test)

distinguishingFeatures: Peripheral neuropathy has nerve conduction abnormalities
Neuropathy typically follows nerve distribution patterns
DVT confirmed by venous duplex ultrasound
DVT has unilateral leg swelling without color/temperature asymmetry pattern of CRPS
Raynaud has episodic digital color changes triggered by cold
Raynaud lacks persistent pain and motor/trophic changes

redFlags: Spreading CRPS to other limbs suggesting central sensitization
Fixed dystonic postures (difficult to treat, poor prognosis)
Severe osteoporosis with pathological fracture risk
Psychological decompensation (high rates of depression, anxiety, suicidal ideation)
references: Harden RN, et al. Validation of proposed diagnostic criteria (the 'Budapest Criteria') for Complex Regional Pain Syndrome. Pain. 2010;150(2):268-274.
Bruehl S. Complex regional pain syndrome. BMJ. 2015;351:h2730.
Goebel A, et al. Complex regional pain syndrome in adults: UK guidelines for diagnosis, referral and management. J Pain Res. 2021;14:1-18.
